style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Clean isometric cutaway illustration, technical drawing style, axonometric projection of a server routing bay in a data hall. Extreme asymmetry, the hero off-centre on the right with generous empty margin on the left. The modular assembly features recognizable aluminum rack modules, glass routing trays, and cobalt cable sheathing arranged in a tiered stack, showing a rigid data pipeline deliberately severed and rerouted into a secondary weathered orange checkpoint tray. Flat muted slate grey palette with weathered orange and cobalt accents, thin consistent line weight, laid over a concrete grey surface. One directional light throwing a long cast shadow.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, labels, UI, people
rationale: The article breaks down the hidden mechanics and metrics of agent restarts. A technical isometric cutaway perfectly captures this systemic, architectural dissection of a software stack's routing and checkpointing logic.
cue: Whether to restart a failing agent run is a purchase
subject: A technical isometric cutaway of a server routing bay showing a diverted processing pipeline
core_thesis: Restart monitors measure accuracy but fail to calculate the true transactional cost of aborting an agent run, which is the subsequent run's chance of finishing with the remaining resources.
core_conflict: Monitor accuracy claims versus the true economic cost of reversing and restarting a software run.
composition: extreme asymmetry, the hero off-centre on the right
alt_text: Isometric cutaway of a server rack whose blue cables route into a wooden crate on a concrete floor.
caption: The pipeline leaves the rack for a crate: the branch a restart discards.
title: The Restart Accuracy Myth
